papers.title: Enhancing cortical electrophysiological signatures of sleep overrides ER stress responses in sleep-deprived mice
papers.summary: In sleep-deprived mice, delivering flickering light stimulation (FLS) during sleep deprivation prevented the upregulation of activity-dependent and unfolded protein response (UPR)/ER-stress genes while further increasing NREM slow-wave activity, and induced brief neuronal OFF periods resembling a sleep-like cortical state. The authors conclude that physiological manipulation of cortical activity can dissociate ER-stress molecular signatures from electrophysiological markers of sleep pressure.

papers.title: REM Sleep Iota Oscillations Across the Lifespan
papers.summary: Analyzed high-density sleep EEG from 937 individuals aged 7–70 and found that iota oscillations during REM sleep peak at 25–40 Hz, increase with REM duration and across sleep cycles, decline in prevalence from 88% in children to 44% in older adults, and show broadened bandwidth with age. Twin analyses indicated high heritability of most iota peak properties except bandwidth, supporting iota as a genetically determined, trait-like REM sleep marker.

papers.title: Sleep reactivation shapes memories of event and its temporal structure
papers.summary: In a preregistered study with 35 participants, closed-loop targeted memory reactivation (TMR) during slow-wave sleep enhanced recognition speed and confidence for cued event memories but impaired temporal-order memory immediately after sleep and attenuated its forgetting one week later. Stronger cue-elicited theta activity predicted better recognition of neutral content and poorer temporal-order memory.

papers.title: Effect of Long-Term Physical Exercise on Memory, Anxiety-Like Behavior, and Depression in Young and Aged Male Mice Subjected to Sleep Deprivation.
papers.summary: Tested whether 8 weeks of treadmill aerobic exercise attenuates behavioral deficits after 72-hour sleep deprivation in young (3-month) and aged (18-month) male mice using Y-maze, tail suspension, and elevated plus maze tests. The authors report that age influences the effectiveness of exercise in mitigating sleep deprivation-induced behavioral deficits.

papers.title: Daytime Napping and Associative-Memory Retrieval Speed: An Exploratory Behavioral and EEG Study
papers.summary: In a within-participant study with 15 healthy students, a 60-min daytime nap was associated with 6.7% faster delayed associative recognition compared to wakefulness, with the effect concentrated among slower responses. EEG showed aperiodic spectral slowing and stronger sigma activity after napping, but no EEG measure explained the response-time effect.

papers.title: Sleep Spindles and Slow Oscillations as Potential Biomarkers and Therapeutic Targets in Mild-to-Moderate Alzheimer's Disease.
papers.summary: Narrative review critically evaluating evidence that sleep spindles, slow oscillations, and their coupling relate to cognition and amyloid/tau biomarkers in mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease, and that closed-loop acoustic stimulation and slow-oscillatory transcranial direct-current stimulation can modify these oscillations. Cognitive and biomarker benefits of stimulation remain uncertain, and biomarker-characterized trials in MCI and AD are needed.

papers.title: A circalunar oscillator and moonlight tune the circadian clock to moon phase via cwo/Dec1
papers.summary: Using transcriptomics, biochemical assays, CRISPR-Cas9 mutagenesis, and behavioral analyses in the annelid Platynereis dumerilii, the study identifies cwo/CWO (a Dec1 homolog) as a key mediator of circadian-circalunidian clock plasticity and shows that cwo is necessary for the clock to adjust to moon phase. A modified Goodwin oscillator model with cwo is sufficient to explain the observed plasticity.

papers.title: Portable polysomnography-derived multi-domain EEG markers of anesthetic state transitions during propofol anesthesia for gastrointestinal endoscopy.
papers.summary: In 31 adults undergoing propofol anesthesia for gastrointestinal endoscopy, portable polysomnography-derived six-channel EEG showed stage-related changes in relative spectral power (delta decreased, theta/alpha/sigma/beta and SEF95 increased), spindle-like event density (highest during recovery), and functional connectivity (most widespread with amplitude envelope correlation). These findings identify candidate EEG markers for anesthetic state transitions.

papers.title: Sleep stage-specific heart rate variability feature-driven clustering analysis: identifying cardiac autonomic endotypes with long-term cardiovascular predictive value.
papers.summary: In 4029 Sleep Heart Health Study participants, the authors applied stage-specific (N2, N3, REM) linear and non-linear HRV features with K-means clustering to derive three phenotypes (Stable, Burden, High risk). The High-risk phenotype was consistently associated with increased incident cardiovascular disease across sleep stages (e.g., N2 HR 1.468, 95% CI 1.280-1.684), with minimal attenuation after adjusting for AHI, ODI, arousal index, and sleep efficiency.

papers.title: The spatial extent of fast ripples is associated with cognitive and language deficits in children with focal epilepsy: An exploratory SEEG study.
papers.summary: In 30 pediatric focal epilepsy patients undergoing SEEG, the spatial extent of interictal fast ripples (250-500 Hz) was significantly associated with cognitive deficit severity (p=0.049), while ripples and interictal discharges were not. Language deficits correlated with fast ripple rates in language-related regions, including Broca's area and its homolog (r=0.66), superior temporal gyrus (r=0.72), and basal temporal region (r=0.79).

papers.title: Sleep Duration and Mental Well-Being Among Older Chinese Adults: A Four-Wave Fixed-Effects Analysis Using CHARLS.
papers.summary: Used four waves of CHARLS (2011–2018) with individual and wave fixed-effects linear regressions to examine within-person associations between nighttime sleep duration and depressive symptoms (CES-D-10) and life satisfaction in older Chinese adults. Each additional sleep hour was associated with lower CES-D-10 scores (β = -0.305) and higher life satisfaction (β = 0.015), while short sleep (≤6 h) was associated with worse mental well-being.

papers.title: Clinical and genetic correlates of a circadian subtype of depression in the Australian Genetics of Depression Study.
papers.journal: The British journal of psychiatry : the journal of mental science
papers.summary: In 2604 participants (23%) of the Australian Genetics of Depression Study, a circadian depression subtype (≥3 circadian features) showed earlier onset, more severe clinical features, poorer SSRI/SNRI response, and higher polygenic risk scores for ADHD, major depression, anxiety, bipolar disorder, BMI, triglycerides, and IL-6. These findings support the face validity and potential clinical utility of a circadian depression subtype.

papers.title: Sleep, inflammation, and pain in musculoskeletal rehabilitation: a structured integrative review of neurobiological mechanisms and non-pharmacological pain management strategies.
papers.summary: This structured integrative review of 57 studies synthesized neurobiological mechanisms linking sleep disturbance, inflammation, and persistent pain, finding sleep restriction associated with changes in IL-6, TNF-α, and CRP and impaired descending pain inhibition. It concluded that exercise, manual therapy, electrical stimulation, laser therapy, and sleep-focused behavioral interventions have mechanistic plausibility but limited confirmatory trial evidence.

papers.title: Beyond the pump: a narrative review of the acute molecular, metabolic, and neuropsychological responses to a bout of resistance exercise.
papers.summary: Narrative review synthesizing acute endocrine, myokine, metabolic, vascular, pain-related, psychological, cognitive, and sleep-related responses to a single bout of resistance exercise. It emphasizes temporally overlapping multisystem effects and cautions that these acute responses should not be assumed to represent adaptive remodeling or direct mechanisms of chronic health benefit.

papers.title: Preoperative sleep deprivation prolongs postoperative hyperalgesia by downregulating spinal cord D2R expression via the PP2A/AKT-dependent NMDA receptor phosphorylation.
papers.summary: In male mice, 48-hour preoperative sleep deprivation aggravated and prolonged post-incisional hyperalgesia through spinal D2R downregulation on glutamatergic neurons, disinhibition of the PP2A/AKT pathway, and increased NMDA receptor phosphorylation; D2R overexpression or PP2A activation with DT-061 produced analgesia.

papers.title: Heart rate rises most during REM sleep after semaglutide initiation: a matched longitudinal cohort study
papers.summary: In a propensity-matched longitudinal cohort (96 semaglutide initiators, 90-94 matched pairs), home sleep studies showed heart rate increases relative to never-users during nocturnal wake (+3.89 bpm), NREM (+4.82 bpm), and REM sleep (+6.25 bpm), with a REM-excess over NREM of 1.42 bpm. The REM heart-rate rise was not explained by weight loss and typically exceeded clinic-measured effects.

papers.title: Integrated Transcriptomic and Single-Cell Sequencing Identifies Altered Expression of Circadian Rhythm-Related Genes Pomc and Bmp4 in Post-Stroke Depression.
papers.summary: Using a photochemical-induced focal cortical lesion PSD model, transcriptomic sequencing identified circadian entrainment gene dysregulation as a central pathway, with six hub genes; single-cell sequencing localized altered Pomc expression to endothelial cells and Bmp4 to oligodendrocytes. In silico perturbation implicated cell adhesion and extracellular matrix interaction as shared regulatory mechanisms.

papers.title: An examination of the effect of dual task on gait in Parkinson's disease and REM sleep behavior disorder.
papers.summary: Comparing 46 RBD, 23 control, and 14 Parkinson's disease participants on gait analysis, the PD group showed greater enhanced gait variability index and dual-task costs for several gait parameters, while RBD converters (6 over 3 years) had greater dual-task costs for functional ambulation performance, velocity, cadence, and double support time than stable RBD.

papers.title: [Neurocognitive characteristics in children with sluggish cognitive tempo].
papers.journal: Zhurnal nevrologii i psikhiatrii imeni S.S. Korsakova
papers.summary: In 40 children with sluggish cognitive tempo (SCT) compared with 30 with combined ADHD and 30 healthy controls, SCT was associated with greater asthenic symptoms, more learning disorders, and a reduced anterior theta-to-alpha EEG power ratio versus ADHD. After Cortexin treatment, 82% showed improvements in inattention, working memory, asthenia, and reading skills, with reduced frontal-central alpha power suggesting enhanced cortical activation.

papers.title: Modification of locomotion-respiration coupling in patients with obstructive sleep apnea syndrome.
papers.summary: In 10 awake OSAS patients on mandibular advancement devices versus 10 matched controls, OSAS patients showed longer double-stance and shorter swing phases and increased phase-locking between inspiratory events and hip/knee motion and between expiratory events and trunk/hip motion. These gait and locomotion-respiration coupling differences disappeared when patients wore their MAD, suggesting reversible adaptive strategies against upper airway collapse.

papers.title: Integrating task-state electroencephalography and motor function for intelligent assessment of recovery status from prolonged disorders of consciousness.
papers.summary: Using task-state EEG and clinical records from 78 patients with prolonged disorders of consciousness, an SVM/logistic regression framework integrating alpha-band power spectral density and coherence measures with motor function scores achieved leave-one-out macro F1 of about 76%, with SHAP used for interpretation. The authors propose this as a preliminary intelligent assessment paradigm for recovery status.

papers.title: [Spectral-topographic features of EEG in patients with varying rates of alcohol dependence progression].
papers.journal: Zhurnal nevrologii i psikhiatrii imeni S.S. Korsakova
papers.summary: In 40 male alcohol-dependent patients, rapid progression (≤3 years, n=23) versus slow progression (≥12 years, n=17) was associated with significantly reduced alpha-1 power across all cortical regions, especially fronto-central, plus reduced alpha-2, theta, and frontal beta-1 power. A low-amplitude flattened EEG pattern occurred in 74% of rapid versus 71% normal alpha rhythm in slow progressors, suggesting a neurophysiological endophenotype.

papers.title: Effects of EEG neurofeedback in adults with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: a systematic review of randomised and non-randomised studies.
papers.summary: This systematic review of 7 studies (3 RCTs, 4 non-randomised; n=390) examined clinical, cognitive, and electrophysiological outcomes of EEG neurofeedback in adult ADHD. RCTs showed small, generally non-significant effects versus controls, while naturalistic and personalised protocols reported large symptom reductions; no treatment-related adverse events occurred.

papers.title: Obstructive sleep apnea is frequent in patients with Long COVID fatigue but is not significantly associated with alterations of quality of life and cognition.
papers.summary: Home sleep testing in 100 consecutive Long COVID patients with fatigue but no prior OSA history found OSA in 53% (33% mild, 20% moderate-to-severe). OSA was not significantly associated with Long COVID symptom burden, quality of life, or objective cognitive function, though 20% with moderate-to-severe OSA warrant intervention.

papers.title: EEG microstate alterations in psychotic depression: prolonged microstate C duration and associations with psychotic symptoms.
papers.summary: Comparing resting-state EEG microstates in 68 patients with psychotic major depression versus 63 with non-psychotic depression, the study found prolonged microstate C duration (91.99 vs 85.56 ms) and altered transition probabilities (increased B→A, decreased B→C and C→A). Reduced B→C transition probability was most strongly associated with thought disturbance (ρ=-0.393) and hostility, suggesting dysregulated perceptual-to-salience network coupling as a candidate marker of psychotic features.

papers.title: Quantitative Analysis of Electroencephalography in Hypnosis: A Neurophysiological Approach.
papers.journal: The International journal of clinical and experimental hypnosis
papers.summary: Reviews EEG evidence on the neural correlates of hypnosis, reporting stronger theta activity in highly hypnotizable individuals, gamma linked to suggestion acceptance and emotional responses, frequency-dependent reorganization of frontal-parietal and attentional networks, and ERP effects at both pre-attentional and cognitive levels. Also reports greater left-hemisphere activity in highly hypnotizable individuals, challenging the right-hemisphere dominance model.

papers.title: Progress in research on the bidirectional relationship between circadian rhythm and depression: A bibliometric analysis.
papers.summary: Bibliometric analysis of 444 Web of Science publications (2015-2025) on circadian rhythms and depression using VOSviewer and CiteSpace, showing markedly increased output after 2018, US leadership, and key themes including expression, sleep, circadian rhythms, and melatonin. The authors identify diagnosis, biomarker identification, individualized treatment, prognosis, and health management as likely future research directions.

papers.title: Persistent postoperative pediatric pain: a secondary analysis of the 4P prospective observational multicenter study.
papers.summary: Secondary analysis of a prospective multicenter cohort of 601 children undergoing common surgeries found persistent postoperative pain in only 3% (13/380 followed at 3-6 months), dropping to 0.8% under a stricter ICD-11-based definition. Pain was usually localized to the surgical site and affected activity in six children, indicating very low PPOP prevalence after common pediatric surgeries.

papers.title: Longitudinal sleep duration trajectories and their association with cardio-renal-metabolic multimorbidity risk in postmenopausal women: evidence from the CHARLS study.
papers.summary: Using 4 repeated sleep measurements (2011-2018) from 2,859 postmenopausal women in CHARLS, group-based trajectory modeling identified normal-stable, normal-fluctuating decline, and short-rapid decline sleep patterns. Relative to normal-stable, the normal-fluctuating decline (OR 2.30) and short-rapid decline (OR 3.75) trajectories independently predicted incident cardio-renal-metabolic multimorbidity.

papers.title: Comparative effects of exercise modalities on sleep quality in middle-aged and older adults with sleep disorders: A systematic review with pairwise, network, and dose-responsemeta-analyses.
papers.journal: Journal of exercise science and fitness
papers.summary: This systematic review with pairwise, network, and dose-response meta-analyses of 23 RCTs (1,478 middle-aged and older adults with sleep disorders) found exercise reduced PSQI and ISI scores but not ESS. Aerobic exercise showed the largest PSQI improvement (SMD 1.34) versus mind-body (0.64) and combined exercise (0.60), with an inverted U-shaped dose-response peaking near 539 MET-min/week.

papers.title: Combined eye tracking and electroencephalography during referential selection in dyadic interaction.
papers.summary: This proof-of-concept study combined mobile EEG and eye tracking with LabStreamingLayer synchronization during a director-task dyadic communication paradigm, computing regression-based ERPs time-locked to spoken nouns and fixations. Targets competing with occluded referents elicited a stronger posterior positivity, fixation timing modulated neural responses, and established artifact-subspace reconstruction, ICA, and linear deconvolution methods proved applicable to naturalistic datasets.

papers.title: Apnea-hypopnea index-oxygen desaturation index (AHI-ODI) discordance in obstructive sleep apnea: association with symptom burden and cardiometabolic comorbidity: A retrospective cross-sectional study.
papers.summary: In a retrospective cross-sectional study of 200 adults with OSA, AHI-ODI discordance was independently but modestly associated with excessive daytime sleepiness (OR 1.04 per event/h) and had the highest but non-significantly different AUC (0.639), while AHI alone was not significant. Oxygenation indices (T90, mean SpO2) were related to prevalent cardiometabolic comorbidity, and the authors conclude AHI-ODI discordance is not a measure of apnea-specific hypoxic burden.

papers.title: [The correlation of interleukin 2 and interleukin 4 with alterations in the brachiocephalic arteries in patients with obstructive sleep apnea].
papers.journal: Zhurnal nevrologii i psikhiatrii imeni S.S. Korsakova
papers.summary: Compared 37 patients with obstructive sleep apnea (AHI>15) to 28 controls, finding chronic cerebral ischemia in 75.7% and brachiocephalic artery atherosclerotic changes in 89.2% of OSA patients, with bilateral increases in common and internal carotid artery diameters and elevated IL-2 along with reduced IL-4. Left and right internal carotid artery diameters correlated positively with IL-4, and atherosclerosis correlated with neck circumference, AHI, hypertension, and chronic cerebral ischemia.

papers.title: Response to Comment on "Melatonin and oxidative DNA damage in REM- and NREM-related obstructive sleep apnea: an exploratory analysis of sleep-stage phenotypes".
papers.journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery
papers.summary: This is a letter responding to a comment on a prior exploratory analysis of melatonin and oxidative DNA damage in REM- and NREM-related obstructive sleep apnea sleep-stage phenotypes; no abstract or new findings are supplied.

papers.title: Comment on "melatonin and oxidative DNA damage in REM- and NREM-related obstructive sleep apnea: an exploratory analysis of sleep-stage phenotypes".
papers.journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery
papers.summary: This letter comments on a published exploratory analysis of melatonin and oxidative DNA damage in REM- and NREM-related obstructive sleep apnea; it contains no abstract or reported findings of its own.

papers.title: [Experience in the implementation of a comprehensive non-pharmacological therapeutic program at the Center for Cognitive and Psycho-Emotional Health].
papers.journal: Zhurnal nevrologii i psikhiatrii imeni S.S. Korsakova
papers.summary: Evaluated a five-day integrated non-pharmacological program (cognitive training, EEG biofeedback, exercise therapy, neurostimulation) in 103 patients stratified by cognitive, psycho-emotional, or sleep complaints; 91.26% showed clinical improvement overall and 96.6% in the psycho-emotional group, with significant cognitive gains and reduced anxiety and depressive symptoms and no deterioration. Gains were nonsignificant in severe cognitive impairment and isolated depressive disorders.

papers.title: Mapping mental health complexity in esports: an exploratory psychosocial network approach.
papers.summary: In a 17-item survey of 1025 esports players analyzed with Directed Acyclic Graph network analysis, game-related thought preoccupation emerged as the most robust sink node, with depressed mood upstream, mental fatigue intermediate, and emotion control/autonomy linking affective distress to esports-specific indicators.

papers.title: Interventions to Address Sleep Disparities in the United States: A Narrative Review.
papers.summary: Narrative review synthesizing 16 studies of interventions addressing sleep disparities among racial and ethnic minoritized, socioeconomically disadvantaged, rural, and urban populations, highlighting tailored messaging, remote/community-based delivery, and stress management. The authors note a lack of intervention research, particularly for individuals with disabilities and sexual and gender minoritized communities, and call for culturally relevant, accessible, scalable solutions.

papers.title: Voluntary wheel running selectively preserves skeletal muscle during pancreatic cancer cachexia despite persistent systemic alterations
papers.summary: Compared voluntary wheel running and treadmill running in UN-KC-6141 pancreatic tumor-bearing mice, finding that voluntary wheel running slowed tumor growth, reduced final tumor mass, and preserved lean and skeletal muscle mass even after adjustment for tumor burden, whereas treadmill running did not. Adipose wasting, hepatic metabolic remodeling, and systemic inflammation remained largely unaffected by exercise.

papers.title: An incidental heterozygous ATP7B nonsense variant leading to a diagnostic pitfall for Wilson disease: a pediatric case report.
papers.summary: A pediatric case report describes a 13-year-old boy with paroxysmal postural instability and dystonic/choreiform movements in whom an incidentally detected heterozygous ATP7B nonsense variant (c.2851C>T; p.Gln951Ter) raised concern for Wilson disease, but normal ceruloplasmin, ceruloplasmin oxidase activity, liver biochemistry, liver ultrasound, and 24-hour urinary copper, plus paternal segregation, made active Wilson disease highly unlikely. The report highlights that interpreting a single heterozygous ATP7B variant outside a compatible phenotype can cause overdiagnosis and diagnostic anchoring bias, emphasizing phenotype-driven evaluation, Leipzig scoring, and biochemical gold standards.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
